grades.reason: Table of contents only. It lists chapter and section titles and gives no reason for keeping one cached buffer per disk block.
Covers the inode layer: itable, reference counts and inode locks. It does not cover the buffer cache or why there is one buffer per disk block.

grades.quote: The buffer cache layer caches disk blocks and synchronizes access to them, making sure that only one kernel process at a time can modify the data stored in any particular block.
grades.reason: The overview says the buffer cache synchronizes access so only one process at a time can modify a block's data. That is the motivation, but it does not say outright that there is only one in-memory copy per block.

grades.quote: synchronize access to disk blocks to ensure that only one copy of a block is in memory and that only one kernel thread at a time uses that copy
grades.reason: Directly answers the question. The buffer cache keeps only one copy of a block in memory so that access can be synchronized and only one kernel thread at a time uses that copy. The per-buffer sleep-lock enforces this.
